market: Corrected from the card's 'stubborn weight after 40': the exhausted woman whose labs came back normal, and the stressed woman who wants one daily stress-and-sleep pill without an appointment. The weight buyer here is a GLP-1 drug shopper, not a reachable AVIA market.
category_they_buy: online prescriptions and telehealth memberships (GLP-1 programmes, Rx hair pills, anxiety Rx, at-home lab panels)
one_line: Hers is a women's telehealth platform selling prescription access (GLP-1 weight loss, minoxidil hair pills, anxiety medication, a 130-marker lab panel) to women who want care online without appointments; it scales by flooding creator UGC (2,242 videos, 40 winners) that sells the access process itself.

customer: the woman who is exhausted all the time, was told her bloodwork is normal, and quietly blames herself for being lazy
customer_words: I needed coffee just to feel like a person. For the afternoon, I was just done.
they ran blood work, and apparently everything was normal

If you're exhausted and no one can tell you why
from_belief: My exhaustion is real and has a cause the standard check missed: I'm not lazy (Labs, m1348352284076838, 83d).
to_belief: One cause a 'normal' day-to-day can hide is a stress rhythm stuck on: cortisol runs my energy clock, and I can support it every morning.
callout: Your bloodwork came back normal. Good. It still doesn't explain 3pm. Stress is a hormone too, and it runs on a morning clock.
why_it_holds: Hers has already taught this buyer that 'normal' does not end the search and that exhaustion is not laziness ('If you're exhausted and no one can tell you why'). AVIA adds one step, from 'a hidden cause' to 'the stress hormone that sets my daily energy', without disputing her labs or her doctor. Balance Blend's 116-day run shows the same buyer accepts 'stress support and sleep in one daily pill', which is AVIA's format.
fit_quotes: I was exhausted all the time. I needed coffee just to feel like a person. For the afternoon, I was just done.

supplements like l-theanine to help reduce stress and sleep issues
If you're exhausted and no one can tell you why
fit_note: Raw match is 18/46 scripts (14 winners), but most hits are category names: 'anxiety' as the Rx being sold (8 scripts), 'thinning'/'hair loss' as the hair product, one 'stress test' (m1035422732437953) and one 'sleeping on hers' (m2385448048660977). Scripts that voice the problem AVIA explains (stress, sleep, exhaustion, afternoon crash) are 6 of 46 (0.13), all winners: Balance Blend x2, Labs x2, hair-from-stress x1, the AI ad's 'unusually tired' x1. Zero scripts say cortisol, cravings, food noise, belly, brain fog, menopause or perimenopause; 'weight' appears twice, both inside GLP-1 ads. The card was right that the Labs 'normal labs, still exhausted' reframe is the strongest hook and that drug comparison is the risk; it was wrong on the market: 'stubborn weight after 40' does not appear, and the weight winners are GLP-1 price ads, 11 of 15 Canadian.

You think that belly bulge is fat? Wrong! It's me!

category_they_buy: stress / meditation / sleep apps (monthly or annual subscription)
one_line: Calm sells a subscription stress app, now led by one feature (EMDR-inspired bilateral audio / 'Deep Rest'), to stressed adults who feel their nervous system won't stand down; it scales on huge test volume (9,529 videos, 232 winners) pushed almost entirely through quiz funnels.
size_read: A big, real market: 2.57M visits/month and 232 winners out of 9.5k videos, with a winner median of 83 days; traffic is flat to slightly down (6-month slope -0.04) while ad output stays very high (3,188 new ads in 30 days).
customer: the burned-out woman who has lost herself: used to be fun and light, now tired all the time, heavy, going through the motions
customer_words: I used to be fun. I used to be spontaneous. I used to be light-hearted and then at some point I just wasn't anymore.
She didn't exist anymore under all of the stress I was dealing with
i was tired before i even started
from_belief: My stress lives in my body and nervous system, not just my head ('a body carrying too much hidden stress').
to_belief: In the body, the stress signal has a messenger, a hormone called cortisol, and I can give that part a morning routine too.
callout: Snapping at everyone isn't a patience problem. It's a stress hormone running on the wrong clock.
why_it_holds: Calm's own ads already moved this buyer from 'mindset' to 'body' ('it's your nervous system responding to chronic pressure'; 'your body won't slow down'). Naming the hormone is one step further down the same road. AVIA's strongest evidence (ashwagandha trials on perceived stress and serum cortisol) sits exactly on this step, and the buyer's words (tired all the time, fog, can't slow down, can't sleep) overlap AVIA's problem list.
fit_quotes: A racing mind is often a body carrying too much hidden stress.
isn't just part of the job, it's your nervous system responding to chronic pressure.
I was tired all the time, heavy. I felt like I was just going through the motions when it came to my own life.
We are looking for people who live with mental fog almost every day and want to regulate their nervous system
fit_note: Corrected by the impression top-up: Calm's #1 and #2 ads by impressions are text reframes ('your nervous system needs a reset, not willpower'; 'reactive behavior is not a flaw, it is biology'). The casting-call ad the lens used ran 151 days but ranks only 248 of 872.
entry_lines: We're looking for women who've tried every way to unwind and still feel wired at night and wiped by 3 pm.
Your nervous system is only half the story. In your body, stress has a messenger: a hormone called cortisol.
This is how I got my mornings back. I kept my wind-down routine. What I added was for the part I couldn't breathe away.
Gentle reminder: tired all day and wired all night isn't just a busy season. It can be a stress hormone that never got the signal to come down.
Notice your jaw. Your shoulders. That tightness is your stress response, and it has a hormone behind it.
Keep the app for your evenings. This is the two-capsule morning for the hormone side of stress.
dont_say: Anything that says apps, meditation or breathing don't work, including Calm's own 'Not meditation, not breathing exercises' contrast turned against them.
'Calms anxiety', 'for anxiety', 'work anxiety relief': anxiety is a disease/diagnosis claim (high risk) for a supplement.
'Regulates' or 'resets your nervous system', 'rewires', 'balances your nervous system': therapy/device language, not structure/function.
Anger, temper, snapping or mood-control promises (the parenting/anger doors) as product outcomes.
Any instant or in-ad effect ('feel it in 60 seconds', 'something shifted the first night', 'tonight').
EMDR, trauma, 'used in therapy' or any borrowed clinical-therapy credibility.
'Detox' as a literal toxin-flush claim; 'lowers cortisol' as a guarantee; use 'supports healthy cortisol levels'.
Weight, belly or menopause outcomes in this audience: the ads never raise them, so they read as a bait-and-switch and add medium-to-high compliance risk.
The Calm name or Deep Rest in AVIA copy; targeting Calm as an interest is fine, naming it in the ad is not.

test_audience: US women 30-55, broad plus interest stack: Calm, Headspace, meditation, mindfulness, burnout, stress management, self-care; exclude existing buyers. If interest targeting is unavailable, run broad with the same creative and read the comments for app mentions.

test_kill: Stop a cell after roughly 3,000-5,000 impressions (or 2x target CPA spent) if hook rate is more than 20% below the control hook and CTR is not above baseline.

category_they_buy: diet programmes & weight-loss apps (points tracking, coaching, workshops; increasingly GLP-1 telehealth)
one_line: WeightWatchers sells a points-based diet programme (app, coaches, community, now GLP-1 access via Med+) to mainstream dieters, and scales on an always-on, claim-free 'new Weight Watchers' brand film cut per market plus app-feature snippets.
size_read: A real, mass market (2.5M visits/month, 154 winners, 1,001 new ads in 30 days), but traffic is falling (6-month slope -0.21) and most long-running winners in the sample are non-US language cuts, so the US reach of what we read is smaller than the headline.
customer: the returning dieter who has 'done WW before', thinks it is outdated, and fell off when she did it alone (the Console card's 'woman 40+ whose diet stopped working', corrected: the ads never name age, menopause or a diet that stopped working)
customer_words: Usually when you do it on your own and you don't know what to eat, that's when everybody falls off.
That's what I do.
from_belief: People fall off when they do it alone; the plan handles the food, support handles the behaviour (with the new 'body and mind' line as a soft second foothold)
to_belief: Part of what pulls me off the plan is my stress hormone; I can support that every morning alongside whatever plan I use
callout: You've got the points, the app and the coach. Nobody gave you anything for the stress.
why_it_holds: WW's own buyers already accept that weight is about behaviour and 'mind', not only food (behavior-science coaches, 'body and mind'). Adding a stress layer is one step, not a fight. But the step rests on the buyer's own experience of stress snacking and on AVIA's ingredient evidence, not on anything WW's ads say: they never mention stress, cortisol, cravings or hormones.
fit_quotes: It's emotionally hard to lose weight. You gaslight yourself into believing, oh, maybe it's me.
Weight Watchers stays with you through the side effects and the plateaus.
fit_note: The card got the market size and the 'it's not just the food' direction right, but the ads do not voice the problem AVIA solves. 0 of 40 winners and 1 of 50 scripts (a 0-day Med+ GLP-1 street interview) use any bridge word; no ad says stress, cortisol, cravings, belly, hormones, menopause or sleep, and none names age 40+. 20 transcripts are missing, but their copy summaries talk recipes, tracking, workouts and 'steady energy' (m3416056448567320, m1545649210599218: soft, not counted), not stress. Most winners are one relaunch brand film in EN/NL/FR cuts. The bridge would rest on the buyer's known belief (WW buyers know they snack under stress), not on what WW has taught them.
entry_lines: I've done the points three times. Nobody once asked me about my stress.
You can eat what you love on your plan. So why do you still reach for it at 3pm?
Myth or fact: stress has nothing to do with the snacks you reach for at night.
If you've ever caught yourself thinking 'maybe it's me', your stress hormone might be part of the story.
Your plan handles the food. This handles the stress. Ten seconds, every morning.
dont_say: 'Diets don't work', 'points don't work', 'apps failed you', or any knock on WW or diet programmes
Any use of the WeightWatchers/WW name, points, ZeroPoint or implied partnership in AVIA ads
Weight-loss numbers or percentages (WW's '29.1%' style quiz stats)
Any GLP-1, Ozempic or medication comparison ('a natural GLP-1', 'without the script')
'#1 doctor-recommended' or invented coaches, doctors or endocrinologists
'Support that actually works' framed as a weight outcome
Targeting copy that asserts personal attributes ('Are you overweight?') per Meta rules

test_kpi: 3-second hook rate and CTR vs AVIA's baseline on the same body; CPA once spend allows
test_kill: Stop if hook rate is >20% under baseline after ~5,000 impressions, or no purchase at 2x target CPA spend

customer: the stressed woman who eats clean, does everything right, and still has the belly, the puffy face and the exhaustion

market: stress hair shedding (Console card); in the ads it is mostly general and genetic hair thinning
category_they_buy: at-home red-light / low-level laser hair-growth devices (alongside serums, topicals and appointments they say they tried)

customer: the woman who catches her thinning hair in a mirror, photo or shower drain (the card's 'woman watching her ponytail thin', confirmed, though her cause is rarely named)

I was looking at photos of myself and I was freaking out about my hair.
it was weak, it was breaking, it was just lifeless overall

callout: You found something for your hair. What are you doing about the year that caused it?
why_it_holds: The buyer in m1963421857641942 already blames her year at work, and m1577043190420332 already lists 'aging stress dht and inflammation' as causes, so stress as a cause is half-installed. AVIA's evidence (KSM-66 ashwagandha, rhodiola, saffron, L-theanine and magnesium studied for stress, sleep and mood) supports the stress half truthfully. It does not support a hair half.
fit_quotes: this past year at work actually broke me a little and my hair was the first thing to show it so much shedding in the shower
every single woman i know who's been through a stressful season like if your hair changed during that time this is a game changer
aging stress dht and inflammation shrink your follicles over time and your hair shows it
